content.title: OpenAI announces it has achieved AGI before 2027? — Discussion
content.text: This market will resolve to "Yes" if OpenAI or an official representative of the company announces that it has created an artificial general intelligence (AGI) by December 31, 2026 ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No". The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from OpenAI and/or its official representative, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.Trader consensus on Polymarket heavily favors "No" at 81.5% implied probability for OpenAI announcing artificial general intelligence (AGI) achievement before 2027, driven by the absence of any official claim amid glaring capability gaps in benchmarks like the newly released ARC-AGI-3, where top models including GPT-5.4 (0.26%), Claude Opus 4.6 (0.25%), and Gemini Pro (0.37%) trail human performance by orders of magnitude at 100%. Recent hype from OpenAI's March 31, 2026, $122 billion funding round at $852 billion valuation—backed by Amazon, Nvidia, and SoftBank, with disputed AGI-tied contingencies—and a team rename to "AGI Deployment" has not translated to demonstrated milestones, fueling skepticism on accelerated timelines. Sam Altman's public roadmaps target AI research interns by 2026 and full AGI researchers by 2028, underscoring persistent scaling challenges; upcoming model releases could shift sentiment, but historical delays temper expectations.This market will resolve to "Yes" if OpenAI or an official representative of the company announces that it has created an artificial general intelligence (AGI) by December 31, 2026 ET.
